meta.titre: National Symbols and Patriotism: what they stand for and how to honour them
meta.sous_theme: Flag, coat of arms, seal, anthem, motto and acts of patriotism

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: On many Monday mornings in schools, and during the 20 May celebrations, pupils stand at attention while the flag is raised and the national anthem is sung. These moments make people feel part of one nation, whatever their language or region. National symbols are the signs that stand for the country and its values, and patriotism is the love and loyalty that citizens show towards it. The GCE asks you to identify each symbol, explain its meaning and describe how a good patriot behaves.

items: A nation is a community of people who share a country, a government and a common future.
Cameroon has two official languages, English and French.
A symbol is an object, a colour, a picture or some words that stand for an idea.

sections.titre: National symbols and the meaning of patriotism
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The national symbols

| Symbol | What it is | What it stands for and where it is used |
|---|---|---|
| Flag | Three vertical bands of green, red and yellow, with a yellow star in the centre of the red band | The identity and sovereignty of the nation; flown on public buildings and at schools and ceremonies |
| Coat of Arms | The official emblem of the State | The authority and sovereignty of the State; it is displayed on official buildings and papers |
| Seal | The official stamp of the Republic | It proves that a government document is genuine, that is, authentic and original |
| Anthem | The official song of the nation, 'O Cameroon, Cradle of Our Forefathers', with verses and a refrain | Sung or played at official ceremonies; people stand at attention to show respect |
| Motto | 'Peace, Work, Fatherland' | The values that guide the nation |

The colours of the flag are usually explained as follows: green for hope and the forests of the south, red for unity, and yellow for the sun and the savannah of the north. The star is a sign of unity.

Days such as National Day on 20 May and Youth Day on 11 February are national celebrations on which the symbols are displayed, but a day is not itself a symbol.

### Patriotism
Patriotism is love for one's country, loyalty to it and readiness to serve it. A patriot shows it by respecting the symbols, obeying the laws, paying taxes, voting, protecting public property, working hard and honestly, refusing corruption, living peacefully with citizens of other regions and languages, protecting the environment and speaking well of the nation. Behaviour that harms the nation, such as corruption, theft of public funds, tribalism or the destruction of public property, is the opposite of patriotism.

### Why this matters
Symbols and patriotism help to unite a diverse people, build pride, encourage citizens to work for development and keep the peace.

variantes.nom: Identifying a symbol from its role
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question describes what a symbol does
variantes.contenu_markdown: Link the job to the symbol: the proof that a state document is genuine belongs to the seal; the song sung at ceremonies is the anthem; the cloth flown on public buildings is the flag; the emblem of the State's authority is the coat of arms; 'Peace, Work, Fatherland' is the motto.

variantes.nom: Writing out a verse or a refrain
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to reproduce part of the anthem
variantes.contenu_markdown: Learn the official text by heart and write it exactly, line by line, with the correct words and spelling. In such questions accuracy is what counts, so do not paraphrase or add words of your own.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how a student or citizen can show patriotism
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give separate actions, each with a reason: respect for the flag and anthem, obedience to laws, honesty, care of public property, peaceful living together. Show that patriotism is lived every day, not only on national holidays.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the model answer to this question: (a) Name two national symbols of Cameroon and state what each one stands for. (b) Explain three ways in which a student can show patriotism. [8 marks]

etapes.justification: 'Name' and 'state' ask for short exact answers, 'explain' needs a reason for each way.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) two symbols with meanings; (b) three explained ways

etapes.justification: Pick symbols whose meaning you are sure of.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The flag and the national motto.

etapes.justification: A symbol is worth marks only if its meaning is given.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The flag stands for the identity and unity of the nation; the motto stands for the values of peace, work and love of the fatherland.

etapes.action: Choose three different ways for the student.
etapes.justification: They should be actions that a student can really do, in school and outside.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Respecting the flag and anthem; obeying school and national rules; protecting public property and working honestly.

etapes.justification: The reason shows why the action expresses love for the country.
etapes.resultat_markdown: These actions build unity, order and pride, which are the aims of patriotism.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
(a) The national flag, made of green, red and yellow bands with a star, stands for the identity and unity of the nation. The national motto, 'Peace, Work, Fatherland', stands for the values that guide the nation.

(b) First, a student shows patriotism by respecting the flag and the anthem, standing at attention during the ceremonies, which honours the nation. Second, a student obeys school rules and the laws of the country, because order is necessary for everyone to live in peace. Third, a student takes care of public property, such as desks and school buildings, and works honestly without cheating, which prepares him or her to serve the country well. In this way patriotism is shown in daily conduct.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'The national motto of Cameroon is Unity and Progress.'
items.pourquoi_faux: This is not the motto. The words are wrongly remembered.
items.correction_markdown: The national motto of Cameroon is 'Peace, Work, Fatherland'.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'The flag is stamped on certificates to prove that they are genuine.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The stamp that proves that a document is genuine is the seal. The flag is a flown emblem of the nation.
items.correction_markdown: The seal certifies government documents; the flag stands for the nation's identity and unity.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Patriotism means only singing the anthem and waving the flag.'
items.pourquoi_faux: These are signs of respect, but patriotism also means daily actions such as honesty, paying taxes and protecting public property.
items.correction_markdown: Patriotism is love and loyalty shown by words and by actions that serve the country.

items.erreur_markdown: A student describes the flag as 'two horizontal bands, one red and one yellow, with two stars'.
items.pourquoi_faux: The description is wrong in layout, colours and number of stars.
items.correction_markdown: The flag has three vertical bands of green, red and yellow, with one yellow star on the red band.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'A patriot must support one political party.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Patriotism is loyalty to the country, not to a party. Citizens may hold different opinions and still love their country.
items.correction_markdown: A patriot serves the nation, respects the law and uses lawful means to express opinions.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Describe the national flag of Cameroon. (b) State the national motto. (c) Name the symbol that is sung or played at official ceremonies.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The flag has three vertical bands of green, red and yellow, with a yellow star in the centre of the red band. (b) The motto is **'Peace, Work, Fatherland'**. (c) The **national anthem**.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain why citizens should respect national symbols, and state two ways in which pupils show that respect in school.
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for developed points.

Why: symbols represent the whole nation and not one person or group; respecting them unites citizens of different languages and regions; they remind people of shared values and history; and they are protected by law.

Ways pupils show respect: standing at attention, silent and still, when the flag is raised and the anthem is sung; learning the anthem and singing it properly; not tearing, soiling or mocking the flag or other emblems; keeping official documents carrying the symbols in good condition.

**National symbols deserve respect because they stand for the whole nation.**

items.enonce_markdown: A classmate says that patriotism is only for soldiers and politicians and has nothing to do with students. Write a reply of about six sentences explaining why he is wrong, with examples of how a student can be a patriot.
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for a clear position, reasons and examples.

Model points: Patriotism is love and loyalty to the country, and every citizen can show it. A student is a patriot by studying hard and honestly, since an educated generation will serve the nation; by obeying school rules and the law; by respecting the flag and the anthem; by protecting public property and keeping the school and the neighbourhood clean; by living peacefully with classmates of other regions and languages; by refusing corruption, cheating and violence. These small daily actions build a united and developing country.

**Patriotism concerns every citizen, including students.**

items_markdown: The national symbols include the flag, the coat of arms, the seal, the anthem and the motto 'Peace, Work, Fatherland'.
The flag has three vertical bands of green, red and yellow and one star on the red band.
The seal authenticates government documents; the anthem is sung at official ceremonies with respect.
National Day is 20 May and Youth Day is 11 February; these days are celebrations, not symbols.
Patriotism is love and loyalty to the country shown by respect for the symbols, obedience to laws, honesty, hard work and care of public property.
Corruption, tribalism and destruction of public property are the opposite of patriotism.
